LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD performs no malicious operations during the execution scope of `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo`. The `source`, `source_x86_64`, and `source_aarch64` arrays define standard downloads from the project's own GitHub repository over HTTPS, which is expected upstream behavior. All sources have SHA-256 checksums defined (none are SKIP), and there is no top-level code execution or command substitution outside of function definitions. The `package()` function contains file extraction and installation logic, but it does not run during these commands due to the `--nobuild`/`--noprepare` flags.

No network requests, obfuscation, or dangerous commands (eval, base64, curl, etc.) are present in the top-level PKGBUILD scope or in any `pkgver()` function. The entire `package()` function is standard for packaging a prebuilt `.deb` archive and does not introduce any supply-chain threats within the scope of these commands.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Standard source downloads with no malicious top-level code execution.</summary>
</security_assessment>
